status.en: 22 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 35% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 22 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 35 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Ethiopian forces have used drones to strike Eritrean troops that were backing Tigrayan rebels, while Eritrean soldiers have crossed into Ethiopian territory, prompting both sides to request UN deterrence or intervention. Ethiopian troops have moved into Adigrat in Tigray near the Eritrean border, and Ethiopia says it is acting in self-defence against Eritrean actions. Eritrea has called on the UN to intervene in the standoff and to take deterrence measures against Ethiopia. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopiske styrker har brukt droner til å angripe eritreiske tropper som støttet tigrayanske opprørere, mens eritreiske soldater har krysset inn i etiopisk territorium, noe som har fått begge sider til å be om FN-avskrekking eller intervensjon. Etiopiske tropper har beveget seg inn i Adigrat i Tigray nær grensen mot Eritrea, og Etiopia sier de handler i selvforsvar mot eritreiske handlinger. Eritrea har oppfordret FN til å gripe inn i fastlåst situasjon og iverksette avskrekkende tiltak mot Etiopia. Konflikten forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
